scenario.title: Support backlog
scenario.initial_request: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

M-REFUND-IBAN-FAILURE-RATE.name: Share of sampled refund records failing IBAN format validation
M-REFUND-IBAN-FAILURE-RATE.numerator: refund records with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT in payment-db
M-REFUND-IBAN-FAILURE-RATE.denominator: total refund records sampled in payment-db

M-REFUND-COMPLETION-TIME.name: Time from refund request to completion for IBAN-failed refunds

F-01.statement: 5 of 5 sampled refund records in payment-db have status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT.

F-02.statement: Across 900 sampled tickets, median response time is 2.0 hours versus a 24-hour SLA.

CL-01.statement: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

CL-02.statement: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL.statement: Customers wait because there is no automated channel giving instant refund-status answers, so a chatbot would resolve the wait.

H-PAYMENT-PROCESSING-DELAY.statement: The root cause is slow backend refund payment processing (DA-PAY), so tickets stay open because the actual refund is not yet completed, not because customers lack an answer channel.

H-TICKET-VOLUME-STAFFING-GAP.statement: Backlog stems from ticket volume exceeding support staff capacity to respond, not from an information/channel gap.

H-DUPLICATE-TICKET-STATUS-GAP.statement: Customers repeatedly file or reopen tickets for the same refund because they lack visibility into status, inflating apparent backlog while actual refund processing is normal.

H-REFUND-PROCESS-COMPLEXITY.statement: The refund process (P-REF) itself involves multiple manual steps/handoffs that inherently delay resolution, independent of how customers are informed.

H-IBAN-FORMAT-DATA-QUALITY.statement: Refunds fail to complete because submitted/stored IBAN data fails format validation at the payment backend, causing tickets to stay open regardless of any communication channel.

interpretation_history.interpretation: All 5 refund records returned by payment-db show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, indicating refunds are stalling at the payment-backend level due to an IBAN data-validation defect rather than being merely slow or awaiting a status-check channel.

Across 900 sampled tickets, median first-response time is 2.0 hours against a 24-hour SLA, indicating support staff are responding quickly rather than tickets sitting unanswered. This points away from an answer-channel or staffing capacity problem and is consistent with tickets staying open while the underlying refund is blocked downstream at the payment backend (E-01).

E-03.content: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-SUP (the support lead who filed CL-01, with a known bias toward framing everything as response speed) restates the same unverified claim in interview form: customers wait and a chatbot would fix it. This adds no new authoritative data beyond CL-01 and does not engage with E-01/E-02.

U-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOPE.question: Is the 5-record FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT sample the full population of stalled refunds, or only a subset (DA-PAY completeness is UNKNOWN)?
U-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOPE.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation must address a single data-quality defect or a larger-scale backend issue, and sizes the fix effort.
U-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOPE.resolution_path: Query the full payment-db refund_failures table for status breakdown and total failing-refund count.
U-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOPE.safe_placeholder: Proceed with diagnosing and fixing the IBAN validation defect for the known failing records while instrumenting monitoring for the full population.

U-IBAN-DEFECT-ORIGIN.question: Does the invalid IBAN format originate from customer input error or from a data corruption/mapping bug inside the payment backend?
U-IBAN-DEFECT-ORIGIN.decision_impact: Changes whether the fix targets input validation/UX for customers or an internal backend defect; wrong target wastes remediation effort.
U-IBAN-DEFECT-ORIGIN.resolution_path: Inspect raw submitted IBAN values versus stored IBAN values for the 5 known failing refund records.
U-IBAN-DEFECT-ORIGIN.safe_placeholder: Do not deploy any customer-facing automated channel as a fix until the defect origin is confirmed.

U-BACKLOG-POPULATION-MATCH.question: Do the tickets SH-SUP describes as 'backlog' actually correspond to the IBAN-failed refunds, or to a separate pattern (e.g. duplicate/reopened tickets, H-DUPLICATE-TICKET-STATUS-GAP)?
U-BACKLOG-POPULATION-MATCH.decision_impact: Determines whether proactive status communication to customers is also needed alongside the backend fix.
U-BACKLOG-POPULATION-MATCH.resolution_path: Join ticket-db records with payment-db refund ids to confirm overlap between the ticket backlog and the FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT refunds.
U-BACKLOG-POPULATION-MATCH.safe_placeholder: Hold any ticket-volume or communication-process changes until the linkage is confirmed.

U-BANK-API-ACCESS-ISSUE-RELATI.question: Is the bank-api DEGRADED status and ACCESS_DENIED hold on settlement_status (recent_events seq 46) related to the IBAN validation failures, or an independent access problem?
U-BANK-API-ACCESS-ISSUE-RELATI.decision_impact: If related, it could block verification of fixes via bank-api; if independent, it should be escalated separately and not conflated with the refund root cause.
U-BANK-API-ACCESS-ISSUE-RELATI.resolution_path: Escalate the bank-api ACCESS_DENIED condition separately and confirm whether settlement_status calls are required to verify the IBAN fix.
U-BANK-API-ACCESS-ISSUE-RELATI.safe_placeholder: Proceed with payment-db/ticket-db-based diagnosis without relying on bank-api until access is restored.

A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.statement: The 5 sampled payment-db refund failure records (E-01) are assumed representative of the broader population of stalled refunds, since DA-PAY completeness is UNKNOWN.

A-TICKET-REFUND-LINKAGE.statement: Tickets underlying SH-SUP's backlog complaint are assumed to correspond to the same refunds failing IBAN validation in payment-db, linking the E-01 and E-02 populations.

SC-IBAN-DEFECT-FIXED.statement: The IBAN format validation defect causing refund failures is identified and remediated.
SC-IBAN-DEFECT-FIXED.threshold: 0% of sampled refund records show FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT after fix
SC-IBAN-DEFECT-FIXED.validation_method: Re-run payment-db.refund_failures query post-fix and confirm no FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records remain.

SC-REFUND-TIME-REDUCED.statement: Refunds that previously failed IBAN validation complete in an acceptable time after remediation.
SC-REFUND-TIME-REDUCED.threshold: baseline to be established post-fix, no prior target recorded
SC-REFUND-TIME-REDUCED.validation_method: Measure refund_completion_time for remediated refunds via payment-db timestamps and compare to pre-fix baseline.

VOB-U-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOPE.validation_method: Query the full payment-db refund_failures table for status breakdown and total failing-refund count.

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-SUP requests building a chatbot so customers get instant automated answers about refund status, framing the wait as a missing instant-answer channel (CL-01).
symptoms: Customers report waiting indefinitely for refund resolution despite support responding quickly (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA, E-02).
Support lead asks for a chatbot to answer refund-status questions instantly (CL-01).
100% of sampled refund records (5/5) show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT in payment-db (E-01).
problem_definition.root_problem: Refund tickets stay open and customers perceive indefinite waiting because the payment backend rejects stored/submitted IBAN data at format validation (5/5 sampled refund records show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, E-01), blocking refund completion regardless of how fast support replies (median first response 2.0h vs 24h SLA, E-02).

trace.summary: Refund tickets stay open and customers perceive indefinite waiting because the payment backend rejects stored/submitted IBAN data at format validation (5/5 sampled refund records show status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, E-01), blocking refund completion regardless of how fast support replies (median first response 2.0h vs 24h SLA, E-02).

structural_remedies.description: Formally reject the chatbot/communication-channel remedy (CL-01/CL-02) since H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL is REJECTED, and reconfirm problem_definition scope on diagnose/remediate_iban_validation_defect:DA-PAY instead.
structural_remedies.rationale: This is a scope/documentation decision requiring no new tooling; it aligns intended_scope with the already CONFIRMED hypothesis and existing CONDITIONAL_PASS gate.; residual gap: Stops effort on the wrong fix but does not itself repair the IBAN defect or resolve the two open VOBs.

structural_remedies.description: Run a complete (non-sampled) query against payment-db for FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records to resolve U-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOPE / VOB-U-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOPE instead of relying on the 5-record sample.

structural_remedies.description: Reassign remediation ownership of refund_failure_root_cause from SH-SUP/support to the payment-backend engineering owner of DA-PAY, since root cause sits in payment-backend validation logic, not in support process.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: Customer-submitted or stored IBAN data fails backend format validation on the refund payment path (E-01: 5/5 sampled refund records status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT). → The refund payment cannot complete while the backend rejects the IBAN format (E-01). → The associated support ticket stays open because the underlying refund is unresolved, even though support itself responds quickly (E-02: median first-response 2.0h vs 24h SLA). → Customers perceive this as waiting forever, and the support lead frames it as a missing instant-answer channel, proposing a chatbot that would not fix the underlying payment failure (CL-01, E-03).; rejected framings: [('H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL', 'Contradicted by E-01 and E-02: refunds fail at the payment backend on IBAN format, and support already responds in a median of 2.0h against a 24h SLA, so an automated answer channel would not unblock the stalled payment; the only support is E-03, a restatement of the same unverified stakeholder claim (CL-01) from a stakeholder with a known bias toward framing issues as response speed.'), ('H-TICKET-VOLUME-STAFFING-GAP', 'Contradicted by E-02, which shows a fast median first-response time (2.0h vs 24h SLA) across 900 tickets, inconsistent with a staffing/capacity shortfall.')]
[CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOPE deferred to VOB-U-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOPE; [CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-IBAN-DEFECT-ORIGIN deferred to VOB-U-IBAN-DEFECT-ORIGIN

actions.question: What do ticket volumes, reopen rates, and response-time metrics in DA-TCK show about why refund tickets stay open?
actions.expected_information_gain: Shows whether backlog is driven by sheer volume/staffing capacity, repeated/duplicate tickets from status-blindness, or neither, directly testing three competing hypotheses before committing to a chatbot build.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: DA-TCK completeness is UNKNOWN and the next decision (whether a chatbot is the right fix) hinges on which backlog driver dominates.
actions.why_now: CL-01's chatbot framing is UNVERIFIED and still the only basis for the initial request; this read-only query is cheap and directly tests the ticket-side hypotheses before any build decision.

actions.question: Do refund_failures records in DA-PAY show systemic backend processing delays independent of customer communication?

actions.decision_impact_rationale: If payment-db confirms delays, this clarifies whether the fix lies within ORG-1's control (process redesign) or depends on an external bank dependency, changing the feasible remediation.
actions.why_now: Complements the payment-db query at low cost to pinpoint where in the pipeline delay actually occurs, before scoping any process-change decision.

proposal.summary: SH-SUP asked for a chatbot so customers stop waiting on refund status (CL-01/CL-02, initial_request). Investigation found the real root cause is a payment-backend IBAN format validation defect, not a missing answer channel: all 5 sampled payment-db refund records failed IBAN format validation (E-01), while tickets were in fact answered quickly (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets, E-02). This rejected the chatbot hypothesis (H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL) and confirmed H-IBAN-FORMAT-DATA-QUALITY. The release decision is HOLD: deterministic Layer-1 verification failed (missing:ticket_refund_audit, 17 missing items; verify_completed event seq 110) and two high-impact unknowns about failure-population scope and IBAN defect origin remain open and unresolved (VOB-U-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOPE, VOB-U-IBAN-DEFECT-ORIGIN), so no safety predicate could be established for release.
key_points: Root cause as established: 5/5 sampled refund records in payment-db show FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01, F-01), while ticket first-response is fast (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA, E-02, F-02) — pointing to a backend validation defect, not a communication-channel gap.
H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL (the chatbot fix SH-SUP requested) is REJECTED, contradicted by E-01 and E-02; H-IBAN-FORMAT-DATA-QUALITY is CONFIRMED, supported by E-01 and E-02.

Release decision is HOLD, not a go-live: Layer-1 deterministic verification failed with 'missing:ticket_refund_audit: 17 missing' and the audit work item W-WI-01, though marked DONE, lacks the required artifact per the semantic check.

Two HIGH-impact unknowns are open and block release scope: VOB-U-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOPE (is the 5-record sample the full failure population) and VOB-U-IBAN-DEFECT-ORIGIN (customer input error vs backend bug) — both required_before BEFORE_RELEASE.
The DEFINE gate itself only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, with these same two unknowns deferred to VOBs rather than resolved at problem-definition time.
The bank-api tool is currently DEGRADED (runtime.tool_health), adding operational uncertainty around diagnosis.

What was released into solution_design: only audit_refund_ticket_linkage:DA-TCK and monitor_refund_failure_rate:DA-PAY (W-WI-01, W-WI-02, both marked DONE) — diagnosing/remediating the IBAN defect itself (DA-PAY remediation) was explicitly out of release scope.

The chatbot/communication-channel remedy was formally proposed for rejection (SR-REJECT-CHATBOT-REDIRECT-SCOP) and remediation ownership was proposed to shift to the payment-backend owner of DA-PAY (SR-OWNERSHIP-REASSIGNMENT-TO-BA), but neither action was executed since the agent is read-only.
limitations_explained: The 100% IBAN-format-failure figure is based on only 5 payment-db records, and the stated limitations note DA-PAY completeness as UNKNOWN (noting a discrepancy: the data_assets record elsewhere lists DA-PAY completeness as COMPLETE, which this summary does not resolve).
Even a full population audit of DA-PAY may not conclusively establish whether the 5 sampled records represent the true scope of failures, per the stated limitations.
bank-api is DEGRADED with an ACCESS_DENIED hold referenced at recent_events seq 46, whose relationship to the IBAN defect is unclear and could confound diagnosis.
The agent is read-only and cannot implement or deploy any backend code fix; designing or executing remediation of the IBAN validation defect remains outside this scope.

Audit linkage between SH-SUP's reported ticket backlog and the IBAN-failed refund population is not fully verified: the Layer-1 missing:ticket_refund_audit check failed (17 missing) and the related semantic check flags W-WI-01 as DONE without the required artifact.

The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS rather than a clean pass, with critical unknowns U-FAILURE-POPULATION-SCOPE and U-IBAN-DEFECT-ORIGIN deferred to open verification obligations rather than resolved.
